column11: Arrowhead's own US list price less the book's Part D gross-to-net convention. List: 'Updated the U.S. wholesale acquisition cost (WAC) of REDEMPLO to $45,000 per patient per year' and 'As part of the One-REDEMPLO unified pricing model, the new price is intended to remain consistent across FCS and severe hypertriglyceridemia (SHTG), if that indication is approved' (Arrowhead fiscal 2026 second quarter release, 2026-05-07, 8-K 0000879407-26-000045, ex. 99.1). The label dose is 25 mg subcutaneously once every 3 months from a prefilled syringe that patients or caregivers are trained to inject (DailyMed setid 7fd37993-f85a-4af1-8bbe-133299f226ed, sections 2.1 and 2.2), so it is a pharmacy-benefit (Part D) product and the Part D convention applies, not the Part B 6% add-on. Gross-to-net 0.5: a gross CMS figure halved lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net annual prices across the nine cycle-one IRA drugs (backend/gross_to_net.py), the rate lly_solbinsiran.csv takes for the same sHTG pool. 45,000 x (1 - 0.5) = 22,500 USD = 0.0225 mm USD

Why not a realised incumbent price, as regn_veopoz.csv's layers use: drug_demand holds no CMS row for Vascepa, Tryngolza or Redemplo (its latest CMS year is 2024, and Redemplo launched in November 2025 per the FY2026 10-K), and Arrowhead quantifies no gross-to-net (FY2026 10-K 0000879407-26-000078 describes 'Gross-to-Net Adjustments' without a figure). column11: Measured on plozasiran itself in sHTG, in a trial, not in practice: Ballantyne CM et al., 'Use of plozasiran across a spectrum of hypertriglyceridemia: long-term efficacy and safety data from the open-label extension period of SHASTA-2 and MUIR trials', Am J Prev Cardiol 2026;27:101523, doi 10.1016/j.ajpc.2026.101523, PMID 42291067, PMC13261268 (NCT05413135), section 3.1: 'Of the 169 subjects from SHASTA-2 who entered this study, 140 (82.8 %) completed the OLE', a 2-year extension at 25 mg every 3 months. SHASTA-2 enrolled fasting triglycerides of 500 to 4000 mg/dL, this layer's population; MUIR (212 of 249, 85.1%) is mixed hyperlipidaemia and is left out. 29 of 169 stopped in 2 years; at a constant hazard, the convention regn_veopoz.csv uses, 1 - (140/169)^(1/2) = 0.0898 a year
column12: A TRIAL FIGURE AND IT READS LOW: these patients had already completed the 48-week double-blind study and chose to continue, the drug was supplied by the sponsor, and there was no prior authorisation, so real-world stopping will be higher. Non-completion counts every exit (the paper reports 26 adverse-event discontinuations, 22 voluntary withdrawals and 5 investigator terminations across both extensions), which is right for one product's stock. Real-world rates the book could use instead: lly_solbinsiran.csv takes 0.182 for the same pool, PCSK9 persistence at 12 months of 81.8% (Blais JE et al., JACC Adv 2026;5:102733, PMID 42000553, PMC13098587), the class this layer's penetration rows are fitted to; and in US commercial claims of 2001 to 2003, new fibrate users had an adjusted 39.9% cumulative discontinuation at one year, no refill within 180 days (Kamal-Bahl SJ et al., Am J Cardiol 2007;99:530-4, PMID 17293198), a free abstract with no free full text, a daily oral generic class and a broad dyslipidaemia population, so not used. The SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 disposition (NEJM 2026;395:1805-17, PMID 42981569) is not freely published
